entries.sense_en: wanted or took a liking to something

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and more formal; a deep wish rather than a passing liking.
synonyms.example: She desired nothing more than peace.

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday word; no sense of a passing whim.
Intense, almost physical need, often for food or attention.

entries.tip_ko: 이 문장에서는 '상상하다'가 아니라 '원하다, 마음에 들어 하다'입니다.

entries.sense_en: happened to someone, usually something bad

synonyms.nuance: Neutral and everyday; can be good or bad.
Sudden and forceful; used for disasters and illnesses.
Literary: a misfortune catches someone before they can escape it.

entries.modern: "a misfortune befell them" → "a misfortune happened to them"

entries.sense_en: because of, by means of

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; simply names the method used.
synonyms.example: He escaped by means of a rope.

synonyms.nuance: Usually for a good cause; dint of can even be used for a bad one, as here.
synonyms.example: Thanks to her help, we won.

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday word with no formal or old-fashioned tone.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 'by dint of hard work(노력 덕분에)'처럼 쓰입니다. 여기서는 나쁜 원인에 쓰인 예외적 용법입니다.

entries.sense_en: extremely bad or severe

synonyms.nuance: Common all-purpose word; dire adds a sense of serious consequences.
Describes a situation with little hope, or a person who feels that way.
Gloomy and unpleasant; less extreme than dire.

entries.tip_ko: 'dire poverty', 'dire warning', 'in dire need'처럼 자주 쓰이는 짝이 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: not loyal; not honest in doing one's duty

synonyms.nuance: Betraying a person or group one owes support to.
Lying or cheating; does not imply a broken promise of loyalty.
Cannot be relied on; describes character, not one act.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서는 주로 '바람을 피우는'이라는 뜻으로 쓰입니다. 여기서는 '믿음을 저버린'입니다.

entries.sense_en: empty, lonely and without people

synonyms.nuance: Emptied of people who used to be there; describes a place, not its mood.
Cold, bare and without hope; often used for weather and landscapes.
Far from other places; neutral and not necessarily sad.

entries.sense_en: an old unit of distance, about three miles

synonyms.nuance: Modern standard unit; a league was roughly three miles.
Metric unit used in most countries; not used in old tales.

entries.tip_ko: 스포츠의 '리그'와 철자는 같지만 여기서는 옛 거리 단위입니다.

entries.sense_en: said that something was caused by something

synonyms.nuance: Says the cause is someone's fault; attribute can be neutral.
synonyms.example: They blamed him for the loss.

synonyms.nuance: More formal; often for qualities or authorship.
synonyms.example: The poem is ascribed to Homer.

synonyms.nuance: Gives someone praise for a good result.
synonyms.example: She credited her teacher for her success.

entries.tip_ko: attribute A to B: 'A를 B의 탓(덕)으로 돌리다'. 명사는 강세가 앞(/ˈætrɪbjut/)에 옵니다.

entries.sense_en: spending too much money on things you do not need

synonyms.nuance: An expensive thing you enjoy; not always a criticism.
Using something badly; does not need to involve money on nice things.
Generous, rich giving or spending; often admiring in tone.

entries.sense_en: gloomy and depressing

synonyms.nuance: Dark or sad; can describe light, weather or a mood.
Dull and lifeless as well as sad.
Suggests unhappiness or unpleasant conditions; also used of people.

entries.sense_en: sad and mournful in mood or look

synonyms.nuance: Sadness for a loss; often used of sounds.
More about a dark, hopeless mood than visible sorrow.
Plainly expresses deep grief; less literary than doleful.

entries.tip_ko: 'dole'(슬픔)에서 온 고어투 단어라 책에서 주로 만납니다.

entries.sense_en: a peaceful, calm state

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday word; also means no war.
Absence of noise or worry; can be brief.
Deep, untroubled peace of mind; a little more poetic.

entries.sense_en: careful and sensible about what might happen

synonyms.nuance: Avoiding risk out of fear; prudent is more about good judgment.
Broader; deep understanding, not just care with risk.
Practical and reasonable in everyday choices.

entries.sense_en: made someone annoyed and a little upset

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for mild irritation.
Repeated small things that wear on your patience.
Emotional hurt or distress; stronger than vex.

entries.sense_en: stayed low with knees bent, close to the ground

synonyms.nuance: Sit on your heels; usually calm and balanced.
Bend forward from the waist while standing or walking.
synonyms.example: He stooped to pick it up.

synonyms.nuance: Draw close, often together with others, for warmth or fear.

entries.sense_en: after a long time; finally

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for the end of a wait or process.
Stresses that it happened after time or effort.
Shows relief after waiting.

entries.tip_ko: 'at length'에는 '길게, 상세하게'(talk at length)라는 다른 뜻도 있으니 문맥으로 구분하세요.

entries.sense_en: a hard stone with colored stripes, used in jewelry

synonyms.nuance: A softer stone, usually smooth and veined, used for floors and statues.
A kind of banded stone, often black and white.

entries.sense_en: made someone feel strong and awake again

synonyms.nuance: Makes someone feel less tired; a lighter effect.
Brings something back to a former good condition.
Medical; bring back from unconsciousness or near death.

entries.sense_en: walking around with no fixed goal

synonyms.nuance: Slow, aimless walking; may be pleasant or lost.
Slow and relaxed walk for pleasure.
Literary; wander over a wide area.

entries.tip_ko: roam은 넓은 지역을 자유롭게 다니는 느낌이 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: thoughtful about other people's needs and feelings

synonyms.nuance: Notices and remembers what others need; very close in meaning.
Broader goodness of heart; considerate is about careful attention.
Follows good manners; may not involve real care.

entries.sense_en: small, delicate and pleasing

synonyms.nuance: Fine and easily broken; dainty adds prettiness.
Very beautiful and finely made; stronger than dainty.
Used for small, slim women or small sizes.

entries.sense_en: a state of very great joy

synonyms.nuance: Everyday, mild-to-strong pleasure.
Literary; joy so strong it carries you away.
Plain, warm happiness; less extreme.

entries.tip_ko: 원문 철자 ecstacies는 옛 표기이고 현재는 ecstasies입니다. in ecstasies는 '황홀해하며'.

entries.sense_en: extremely beautiful and delicate

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and warm; less strong than exquisite.
Graceful and stylish in shape or manner.
Casual, very attractive; bolder and showier.

entries.sense_en: rude, disrespectful behavior toward someone with authority

synonyms.nuance: General bad manners; no sense of defying authority.
Bold, cheeky disrespect, often from someone younger or lower.
British informal; mild, sometimes playful.

entries.sense_en: a very large amount of money

synonyms.nuance: Common word for a huge sum; also means luck.
Casual; a very high price.
Informal idiom for a price that hurts.
synonyms.example: It cost an arm and a leg.

entries.tip_ko: ransom은 원래 '인질 몸값'입니다. 왕의 몸값처럼 큰돈이라는 뜻.

entries.sense_en: get or buy something, often with effort

synonyms.nuance: Formal; get by asking or effort.
Everyday and informal; no sense of effort.
Formal; gradually gain, often skills or property.

entries.sense_en: in a stern, serious and unfriendly way

synonyms.nuance: Strict and disapproving, like a judge.
Bad-tempered and bitter.
Serious because of an important matter, not anger.

entries.sense_en: in a modest, respectful way, showing no pride

synonyms.nuance: Quietly and without resistance; a bit weak.
Not boasting about oneself.
Shows regard for another person's rank or age.

entries.sense_en: a loose sleeveless cloak worn over other clothes

synonyms.nuance: Most common word; a long loose outer garment.
Shorter than a cloak, often hanging from the shoulders.
A piece of cloth worn over shoulders, usually for warmth.

entries.sense_en: cried out or complained in grief

synonyms.nuance: Feel or show sorrow, especially for a death.
Cry out loudly and long.
Express annoyance; without deep sorrow.

entries.sense_en: foolish behavior or a foolish act

synonyms.nuance: Plain word; general lack of sense.
Harsher; lack of intelligence.
Extreme foolishness, as if crazy.
synonyms.example: It would be madness to go.

entries.sense_en: lit up with many lights

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrasal verb.
Make brighter; not necessarily fully lit.
Adds ornaments; lights are only one possible kind.

entries.sense_en: an animal hunted and eaten by another

synonyms.nuance: A person or animal harmed; not necessarily hunted for food.
The animal or person being hunted or chased.
Anything aimed at, not just living things.

entries.sense_en: worry and sadness at something unwelcome

synonyms.nuance: Sudden fear about danger.
synonyms.example: She felt alarm at the noise.

synonyms.nuance: Sadness that hopes were not met; milder.
Deep worry or pain; stronger.

entries.tip_ko: with dismay, in dismay로 자주 쓰입니다.

entries.sense_en: amazed and almost blinded by brightness or beauty

synonyms.nuance: Surprise greatly; no idea of brightness.
Literally stop someone from seeing, often for a short time.
Win admiration; milder and less bright.

entries.sense_en: satisfied or granted

synonyms.nuance: General; meet a need or demand.
Carry out a promise, dream or duty.
Allow oneself or someone a pleasure, maybe too much.

entries.modern: "Your every wish shall be gratified" → "Every wish you have will be granted"

entries.sense_en: changed in appearance to hide who someone is

synonyms.nuance: General; cover or keep out of sight.
Cover the face or feelings with something.
Blend into surroundings, especially animals or soldiers.

entries.tip_ko: 'no matter how I may be disguised'는 '내가 어떤 모습으로 변장했더라도'입니다.

entries.sense_en: grand, dignified and impressive

synonyms.nuance: Beautiful and powerful, like a king or mountain.
Calm and serious in manner, worthy of respect.
Large and impressive; more casual.

entries.sense_en: in a rough, low voice, sounding unfriendly

synonyms.nuance: Unkind and severe; gruff can hide real kindness.
Short and rude in few words.
Not gentle; can describe voice or actions.

entries.tip_ko: gruff는 겉은 퉁명스러워도 속은 다정한 사람에게 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: fierce and violent-looking

synonyms.nuance: Strong and aggressive; also for weather and competition.
Cruel and wild; suggests violence without control.
Intentionally cruel or spiteful.

entries.sense_en: made someone angry

synonyms.nuance: Plainly make someone angry.
Annoy mildly; provoke may cause an angry reaction.
Annoy in a playful way.

entries.sense_en: a large cage or building where birds are kept

synonyms.nuance: A small cage for one or a few birds.
A cage for chickens and farm birds.

entries.sense_en: a show told through actions, music and dance

synonyms.nuance: Acting without words; pantomime here includes music and dance.
General word for any performance.
A grand, impressive sight.

entries.tip_ko: 영국에서는 크리스마스 시즌의 가족 뮤지컬 코미디도 pantomime(panto)이라 부릅니다.

entries.sense_en: confusing and hard to understand

synonyms.nuance: Like a puzzle: you keep wondering how to solve it.
Unclear or mixed up; more common.
Impossible to understand at all; stronger.

entries.tip_ko: perplexed는 사람이, perplexing은 상황이 주어일 때 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: in a sad and mournful way

synonyms.nuance: Plain, general word.
With the sound or look of grief.
In a dark, hopeless mood.

entries.sense_en: feel sorry for something you did or failed to do

synonyms.nuance: Common; feel sad about a past act or choice.
Literary; regret bitterly.
Say sorry out loud; repent is inner feeling.

entries.modern: "you may have cause to repent it" → "you may regret it"

entries.sense_en: hurried to do something

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word.
Faster and more panicked, often careless.
Move or make happen faster.

entries.sense_en: in a way that shows you think someone did wrong

synonyms.nuance: Shows you blame someone for a specific act.
Shows you think it is wrong, without hurt feelings.
With deep resentment.

entries.sense_en: angrily because something seems unfair

synonyms.nuance: General anger with any cause.
Bitter over a long time.
Extreme anger.

entries.tip_ko: indignant는 부당한 대우에 화날 때 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: delay doing something

synonyms.nuance: Formal; move an event to a later time.
Make something late; may be unplanned.
Keep delaying out of laziness or fear.

entries.tip_ko: put off는 '~를 불쾌하게 하다'라는 다른 뜻도 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: told someone, with hurt or disappointment, that they had done wrong

synonyms.nuance: Angry words, as to a child.
Formal, sharp criticism.
Say something is someone's fault.

entries.sense_en: come back to consciousness

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrasal verb for waking after fainting.
Get better after illness or shock over time.
Stop sleeping; no sense of near death.

entries.sense_en: a magic spell

synonyms.nuance: Common; words or actions that cast magic.
A spell meant to bring harm.
A small or pleasant magic; also personal appeal.
